name: Contract Marriage
blurb: A one-year marriage on paper, no feelings, and one sealed clause she must not open
title: Contract Marriage: Romance Short Drama Script (Episode 1)
description: A free 2.5-minute vertical romance short drama script for 4 actors. Two adults sign a one-year marriage contract; one sealed clause hides a secret.
h1: Contract Marriage: a 2.5-Minute Romance Short Drama Script, Episode 1
logline: Iris needs a roof and a loan paid off; Leo needs a wife before his father's sixtieth birthday. Their one-year contract is all business, until Leo adds a sealed twelfth clause and keeps knowing things about her he should not know.
setting: A café table and a small flat (living room and bedroom). Props: a printed contract, a sealed envelope, a suitcase, a pot plant, two cups of tea with lemon, a cake box, a lamp.

roles.name: Iris
roles.note: Early 30s, a cook with a restaurant loan and an eviction letter; proud, funny, hates owing anyone.

roles.name: Leo
roles.note: Early 30s, polite and guarded; agreed to the contract for reasons he does not say.

roles.name: Nadia
roles.note: Any age 25 to 40, Iris's best friend; nosy comic relief. Any gender.

roles.name: Grace
roles.note: 20s, Leo's younger sister; warm, loud, says too much.

script.action: IRIS, early thirties, in a chef's jacket under her coat, slaps a printed contract on the table in front of LEO, early thirties, neat, unreadable.

script.say: One year. Separate rooms. No feelings. Sign here.
I read it last night. Twice. I want to add one clause.
Of course you do.

script.action: Leo takes a sealed envelope from his jacket and lays it on the contract.

script.say: Clause twelve is in here. You open it on the last day of the contract. Not before.
And if I don't like it?
Then you walk away a free woman with your debt paid. That's the deal.

script.action: Iris hesitates, then signs. Leo signs under her name. They shake hands like business partners.

script.scene: INT. LEO'S FLAT – LIVING ROOM – EVENING

script.action: Iris drags in one suitcase. NADIA, her best friend, carries a pot plant and looks around like a detective.

script.say: He has a spare room, a quiet street, and his father hands him the family bakery the moment he's married. You have an eviction letter and a restaurant loan. Very romantic.
It's practical. His father turns sixty on Saturday. I show up, smile, eat cake, go home to my own room.
And why you? He could pay an actress.

script.action: Iris opens her mouth. Closes it. She doesn't know.
Leo enters with tea. He puts a cup in front of Iris: no sugar, a slice of lemon. Exactly how she takes it.

script.say: I never told you how I drink my tea.
Lucky guess.
You also knew my loan was forty-one thousand. To the exact number. I told nobody that. Not even Nadia.
Not even Nadia!
Is that a problem for the contract?
It is if my husband is a stranger who knows more about me than I do.

script.action: The doorbell rings. GRACE, Leo's younger sister, breezes in with a cake box, sees Iris, and stops dead.

script.say: Oh my word. It's really you.
Have we met?
No, but I've seen your face every day for ten years. It's on his desk. Leo, you actually found her?
Grace. Kitchen. Now.

script.action: Leo steers Grace out. Nadia and Iris stare at each other.

script.say: Iris. That's not a contract marriage. That's a mission.

script.scene: INT. LEO'S FLAT – SPARE ROOM – NIGHT

script.action: Iris sits on the bed, the sealed envelope in her hands. She holds it up to the bedside lamp. Through the paper, a few lines of handwriting show.
Not Leo's writing. Round and childish. She traces it with a finger and goes pale.

script.say: That's my handwriting.

script.action: A soft knock on the door.

script.say: Iris? You're not opening it, are you?
Leo. Why do you have a letter I wrote when I was nine?

body: Shoot vertical 9:16 with the phone on a small tripod at table height for the café, and handheld in the flat so it feels more personal. A café corner at a quiet hour or a kitchen table works for scene one. For the lamp shot, turn off every other light and hold a sheet of paper with pencil writing on the back against a bright bulb; test it first so the writing really shows. Record room sound with the phone close to the actors, and do at least three takes of the tea beat, playing Leo's lucky guess differently each time.

ul: Iris and Leo play the first scene as a business meeting. No smiles, no lingering looks; the romance has to sneak in later.
Leo is not cold, he is careful. Every line he says is the shortest true thing he can say without giving himself away.
The tea moment is silent acting: let Iris look at the cup, then at Leo, before she speaks. Pause longer than feels comfortable.
Nadia gets the laughs. Her offended Not even Nadia must be quick and real, then she drops back into whispering.
Grace should believe she is delivering happy news. Her joy is what makes the reveal awkward.
Whisper the last two lines but keep them clear; the final question is the cliffhanger and must be heard.
Set it in a family-run shop instead of a flat: the contract is signed over the counter, and the sister walks in from the stockroom.
Swap the roles so Leo is the one being evicted and Iris needs a husband to take over her family's business.
Change the hook for part two: the letter inside the envelope is not from Iris at all, but signed with her name by someone else.

faq.q: Is this script free to use in a short drama series?
faq.a: Yes. It is licensed CC BY 4.0, so you can film it, extend it into a full series and post it on monetised channels. Credit "Script: cv.cm" in the description or end card.

faq.q: What is in the sealed clause twelve?
faq.a: The episode only shows that the envelope holds a letter Iris wrote as a child. The obvious next step is a childhood meeting she has forgotten and Leo has not, but you can decide what happened and why he kept it.

faq.q: How long does it take to rehearse?
faq.a: About an hour. Read it twice at the table, then walk the three scenes. Spend most of the time on the tea moment and the final whisper; those two beats carry the whole episode.
